jobs.objective: PROPOSE the falsifiable RFC 0136 implementation SPEC: range-partition the owner-held append-only chained tables `events` and `audit_log` by `created_at`, with partition DETACH/DROP as the retention path that subsumes #386. Read the v1 SEED and RFC 0136 in full first. The hard core to PROVE: declarative range partitioning FORCES a PK/unique-key reshape on these two tables, and that reshape preserves every existing integrity guarantee. Specify each as a FALSIFIABLE assertion + the test that would refute it: (1) the PK reshape — `events` PK `(repository_id, event_id)` and `audit_log` PK `(audit_id)` + `row_hash UNIQUE` must gain `created_at` to be partition-legal (Postgres requires the partition key in every unique constraint), WITHOUT breaking the six `events` FKs, the `audit_log` `segment_id` FK, or `audit_segments`/`audit_chain_head`; (2) the DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FK `repo_event_chain_heads (repository_id, last_event_id) -> events(repository_id, event_id)` (0006:72) must still resolve across partitions; (3) the in-DB hash chain (`append_event_row`/`event_v3_row_hash`; `append_audit_row`/`audit_v3_row_hash`) and the append-only triggers (`events_no_update`/`events_no_delete`; `audit_log_no_update`/`audit_log_no_delete`) must remain intact and chain-correct across partition boundaries; (4) OWNER-DDL DISCIPLINE — the reshape is owner DDL (owner bundle 0020, re-fetch the next-free ordinal per D236/D239), NEVER a runtime migration (the `TestFutureRuntimeMigrationsDoNotCarryOwnerDDL` guard + the D187/#244 two-role crash-loop); (5) partition DETACH/DROP retention SUBSUMES #386 (the delete-time RI seq-scan does not happen at all for the retention path). Be explicit about the DEPENDENCY on 0142 P5 (the highest-risk owner-DDL reshape is un-rehearsable without P5's ephemeral two-role clone + expand/contract) — state what P0 of this design can specify ahead of P5 and what must wait for P5's rehearsal harness. Anchor every claim to the named source. Keep the local-first boundary. This is the published claim the falsifiers re-attack.
jobs.title: Hold leading proposal

jobs.objective: Read the published holder SPEC and RFC 0136. Your lens is RESHAPE CORRECTNESS + CHAIN/RI INTEGRITY. Attack: does the PK/unique-key reshape (adding `created_at`) actually preserve every constraint — can the six `events` FKs, the `audit_log` `segment_id` FK, and the DEFERRABLE chain-head FK to `events(repository_id, event_id)` still resolve once the parent is partitioned (Postgres FK-to-partitioned-table and cross-partition unique semantics)? Does the in-DB hash chain stay correct across a partition boundary — can `append_event_row`/`append_audit_row` advance `repo_event_chain_heads`/`audit_chain_head` correctly when the latest row and its predecessor land in different partitions, and do the append-only `no_update`/`no_delete` triggers still fire on every partition? Does adding `created_at` to the PK change row identity / break any existing query or covering index (#386 `0015`)? Is there a window during the reshape where the chain can fork or a duplicate `row_hash` slip in? Construct the failing case for each. If the reshape breaks an FK, the hash chain, an append-only guarantee, or row identity, say so explicitly and stop the gate from clearing.
jobs.title: Falsifier 1 (reshape/chain-integrity lens)

jobs.objective: Read the published holder SPEC and RFC 0136. Your lens is OWNER-DDL SAFETY + RETENTION + the 0142 P5 DEPENDENCY. Attack: is the reshape correctly an owner bundle (0020, next-free re-fetched) and NOT a runtime migration — would it trip `TestFutureRuntimeMigrationsDoNotCarryOwnerDDL` or crash-loop a two-role production daemon (D187/#244)? Is the ALTER-to-partitioned-table mechanism actually executable on the ~13.5M-row `events` table without an unbounded exclusive-lock outage, or does it need a P5-style expand/contract / shadow-table migration (and is THAT rehearsable only under 0142 P5)? Does partition DETACH/DROP as retention genuinely SUBSUME #386 (no delete-time RI seq-scan), and does dropping a partition respect the append-only triggers + the hash chain (you cannot DROP a chained segment without breaking verifiability)? Is the reshape REHEARSABLE — the RFC itself says the highest-risk owner DDL is un-rehearsable without 0142 P5; does the SPEC honestly scope what is designable now vs gated on P5, or does it over-claim build-readiness ahead of its blocker? Construct the failing case for each. If the reshape is unsafe as owner DDL, the retention path breaks the chain, or it over-claims readiness ahead of P5, say so explicitly and stop the gate from clearing.
jobs.title: Falsifier 2 (owner-DDL/retention/P5-dependency lens)

jobs.objective: Read only the dialogue trajectory for the RFC 0136 design (the holder SPEC and the two FALSIFIER challenges), with RFC 0136 as context. Publish the collaboration ledger verdict (accept / accept_with_findings / needs_revision / reject — a clearing verdict is accept or accept_with_findings, never `clear`). A clearing verdict REQUIRES: the PK/unique-key reshape preserves every FK (incl. the DEFERRABLE chain-head FK), the in-DB hash chain, the append-only triggers, and row identity across partitions; the reshape is correctly OWNER DDL (bundle 0020) that will not crash-loop a two-role daemon; partition DETACH/DROP retention subsumes #386 without breaking the chain; and the SPEC HONESTLY scopes what is designable now vs gated on 0142 P5's rehearsal harness (no over-claim of build-readiness ahead of its blocker). Record per claim whether HELD and per falsifier challenge whether it STANDS or is REBUTTED. needs_revision if any integrity guarantee breaks, the owner-DDL safety is unproven, the retention path breaks the chain, or the SPEC over-claims readiness ahead of P5. This is the single allowed v1 revision cycle; a second needs_revision ends the gate unCleared and routes to the operator (who spins a fresh -v2 run with a revising holder).
jobs.title: Adjudicate dialogue substance

jobs.objective: Publish the cleared, falsifiable RFC 0136 implementation SPEC — ONLY after the adjudicator ledger records a clearing verdict — consolidating the design buildable contract-first by the rfc-0136-build code_change run (gated on 0142 P5): the PK/unique-key reshape on `events` + `audit_log` (adding `created_at`, all FKs/chain-head FK/hash chain/append-only triggers preserved), the owner bundle 0020 (next-free re-fetched) carrying the reshape, the partition DETACH/DROP retention path subsuming #386, and the explicit P5-rehearsal dependency boundary (what lands now vs after P5's ephemeral two-role clone + expand/contract). State each as a falsifiable assertion + its test, anchored to the named source. Note the migration/owner-bundle and the P5 gate. Reference the clearing ledger. This consolidated SPEC is the single source the build run implements.
